title: Lord, in Heaven, Thy Dwelling-place
description: Lord, in Heaven, Thy Dwelling-place in Tonic Solfa to HOLLINGSIDE, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: John Bowring wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 54, “Lowly Praise”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens Double (7.7.7.7 D) (7.7.7.7.7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to HOLLINGSIDE; any other Sevens Double (7.7.7.7 D) tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lord, in heaven, Thy dwell-ing place, Hear the prais-es of our race, And, while hear-ing, let Thy grace Dews of sweet for-give-ness pour; While we know, be-nig-nant King, That the prais-es which we bring Are a fee-ble of-fer-ing, Till Thy bless-ing makes it more.

lines: Hear the praises of our race,
And, while hearing, let Thy grace
That the praises which we bring
Till Thy blessing makes it more.
More of truth, and more of might,
More of love, and more of light,
More of reason, and of right
From Thy pardoning grace be given!
This can make the humblest song
As the strains the angels' throng
Pour around the throne of heaven.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: John Bowring died in 1872.
credits: Words by John Bowring (1792–1872), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to HOLLINGSIDE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
